Jane Andrews possesses an appearance that is described as neat, sensible, and plain.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Autumn P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Jane Andrews is a steady, sensible, and lady-like individual known for her unflappable nerves and practical outlook. Initially committed to devoting her life to teaching for a salary rather than marrying, she eventually resigns her teaching position with plans to head West in the fall. She is also skilled at cooking, though her husband does not allow her to do it.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. ## History

Jane Andrews attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md) after belonging to a childhood schoolgirl [Story Club](../codex/factions.md#story-club) together. On the final day of school, Jane cried so much over her departing teacher's farewell speech that she had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother. After earning a spot on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, she worked as a teacher at [Newbridge](../codex/places.md#newbridge) school, earning the fondness of the local community. Later, she resigned from her subsequent teaching job at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school and went to teach on the western prairies. Jane remained close friends with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), accompanying her to a charity concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), going on scenic nature walks, and joining her in canvassing local residents for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers). On behalf of her shy brother [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md), Jane delivered a marriage proposal to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md); when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) turned down the offer, Jane reacted coldly. She eventually became engaged herself in a lavish affair, leaving her home behind as her old friends moved into new stages of life.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P0](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P15](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0015), [v1 CHAPTER XXI. The Hotel Concert P28](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0028), +28 more_

## Quotes

> “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)
